liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Shakedown Street** (1 review): The reviewer considers this opener one of their favorite versions of the song [18]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): The reviewer specifically recommends checking out the performance of this song [21]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): This set-closing song is cited as one of the reviewer's favorite versions [18]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): The reviewer notes that Jerry could really sing during this performance [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-03-13.132621.aud.sennheiser421.flac24** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 176 min [1]
- **gd1981-03-13.175256.sbd.miller.remaster.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 183 min [3]
- **gd1981-03-13.147852.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 185 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1981-03-13.174927.aud.Bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 176 min [5]
- **gd1981-03-13.wise.lutch.4167.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 176 min; rated 4.3/5 by 23 [8]. Said about its sound: The audience recording features very good sound quality for an early 80s tape; The audience recording captures high energy and audience response, with added bass [17][20]

## Around the show

- Friends from Rockport attended this show, which was the reviewer's first Dead concert [18]
- The band performed with high energy during crazy upstate March weather [20]
- Utica in March is described as cold, snowy, and steely grey [24]
- A Steal Your Face sign was visible over the stage in the rear [28]
- The band played on a stage that looked like a flat bed trailer [28]
- The show is described as a gem, comparable to the best performances from 1981 onward [19]
- The reviewer suggests this might be the best show of the east-coast tour [21]
- The show is part of a great winter-spring 1981 run for the band [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-03-13.132621.aud.sennheiser421.flac24**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Cassette Audience Master recorded by Jim Wise; Sennheiser MD 421 mic's mounted on a stand- Sony TC D-5 Cassette Recorder; Location @ Soundboard; Analog to… [1]. Also: The recording is a Sennheiser 421 audience source, patched with other sources [1]
- **gd1981-03-13.175256.sbd.miller.remaster.flac1644**: transferred by Remastered by Charlie Miller  November 22, 2025; source: Set 1: SBD > Cassette Master > Reel > DAT (shnid=113101) Set 2: SBD > Old Mono Cassette (shnid=33336) [3]. Also: The Set 1 soundboard vocal phase issue was repaired by the uploader; Significant work was done on the Set 2 soundboard recording [3]
- **gd1981-03-13.147852.fob.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics (with bass EQ)> Sony D5M (dolby B)(Maxell XLIIS) [4]. Also: Charlie Miller handled the transfer and coordinated the release effort; The Sennheiser 421 source supplies patches for Music Never Stopped and the encore [4]
- **gd1981-03-13.174927.aud.Bernstein.ackerman.noel.flac2496**: taped by Master Cassettes Recorded by Jon Bernstein; transferred by Transfer by Ray Ackerman Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel September 30, 2025; source: ?? mics > ?? lead deck > ?? Deck > Master Cassettes [5]. Also: Jon Bernstein recorded the show, with the taper positioned centered and upfront [5]
- **gd1981-03-13.wise.lutch.4167.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise and Jamie Lutch; source: Senn 421 > D5 > MAC > Nakamichi Dragon > A/D Conversion via Sony R700 (no DAT gen) > COAX to ZA2 > Soundforge > Master CDR [8]. Also: The source is an audience recording, not a soundboard recording [22]
